cards.title: Exponent Rule-Corrected Allometry (ROE) Methodology
cards.claim: Exponent rule-corrected allometry (ROE) is an empirical candidate that selects a correction based on the fitted simple-allometry exponent b: in the cited rule, no correction for b < 0.71, MLP correction for 0.71 ≤ b < 1, and BRW correction for b ≥ 1. These cutoffs define that historical method; they are not universal physiological boundaries or guarantees of predictive improvement.
conditions: Multiple species data available for simple allometry fit.
Exponent b is calculated from the log CL vs log BW regression.
Species-specific MLP and BRW values are available.
limitations: The source did not show universal benefit for macromolecules or renally eliminated small molecules.
Low-clearance hepatic compounds can remain poorly predicted; compare alternatives and report uncertainty.
cards.downstream_use: Evaluate ROE as one documented empirical scaling candidate when its assumptions and species data are applicable, without treating its cutoffs as mandatory project policy.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
